He did not say "war from Allah and His Messenger" (bi-harbi Allahi wa-rasulihi), because this is more eloquent, since the meaning is: then be informed of a kind of great war from Allah and His Messenger. It is related that when this was revealed, Thaqif said: "We have no power for war against Allah and His Messenger."

﴿And if you repent﴾ from usury (al-irtibaa') ﴿then you shall have your capitals; you do not wrong﴾ the debtors by seeking an increase over them.

﴿Nor are you wronged﴾ by any reduction from them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 280:

﴿And if he is in hardship﴾ — that is, if one of your debtors is in hardship, ﴿dhū ʿusrah﴾, meaning one who is in straitened circumstances (iʿsār).

﴿then let there be postponement﴾ — i.e., the ruling, or the command, is postponement (naẓirah), meaning granting respite (inẓār).

﴿until a time of ease﴾ — until prosperity (yasār). Maysarah is read by Nafiʿ, and both are dialectal variants (lughatān).

﴿And that you remit it as charity﴾ — read with the lighter form (takhfīf) by ʿĀṣim, meaning: that you give charity with your capital, or with part of it, to the debtor who is in hardship. Others read it with the doubled form (tashdīd). The lighter form is based on the deletion of one of the two tāʾs, and the doubled form is based on assimilation (idghām).

﴿is better for you﴾ — in the Resurrection. It has also been said that by "charity" is meant granting respite (inẓār), based on the saying of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: "The debt of a Muslim man is not due, and he postpones it, except that he will have a charity for every day," ﴿if you knew﴾ — that it is better for you, so that you would act upon it. He who does not act upon it, even though he knows it, is treated as if he did not know it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 281:

﴿And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah﴾. "Turju'un" (you will be returned) is read by Abu 'Amr as "yurja'un" (in the form of "rajaʿa", which is both intransitive, "to return", and transitive, "to cause to return"). It was said: this is the last verse that Jibril (peace be upon him) brought down, and he said: "Place it at the head of the two hundred and eightieth [verse] of al-Baqarah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) lived after it twenty-one days, or eighty-one days, or seven days, or three hours.

﴿Then every soul will be paid in full what it earned﴾, that is: the recompense of what it earned.

﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ by a reduction of good deeds or an increase in evil deeds.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 282:**

﴿O you who have believed, when you contract a debt with one another﴾: that is, when some of you deal with others on credit. It is said: "I dayantu (I lent on credit) the man," when I dealt with him on credit, whether as the giver or the taker.

﴿for a specified term﴾: a known period, such as the harvest, the threshing, or the return of the pilgrims. The mention of "debt" was needed, rather than saying "when you contract for a specified term," so that the pronoun would refer to it in His words ﴿then write it down﴾. Had it not been mentioned, it would have been necessary to say, "then write down the debt," and the composition would not have had that beauty. It is also because it is clearer in distinguishing debts into deferred (mu'ajjal) and immediate (hall). He commanded the writing of the debt because that is more secure, safer from forgetfulness, and further from denial. The meaning is: when you deal in a deferred debt, then write it down. The command is one of recommendation (nadb). It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the intended meaning is the salam (advance sale, in which the price is paid now and the goods are delivered later). He said: "When Allah prohibited usury, He permitted the salam, a guaranteed debt for a known term, in His Book, and He revealed concerning it the longest verse." In it is evidence that a term must be stipulated in the salam.

﴿And let a scribe write it between you﴾: between the two parties to the debt, ﴿a scribe with justice﴾. The phrase "with justice" is connected to "scribe" as a description of him. That is, a scribe trusted regarding what he writes, who writes with caution, neither adding to what must be written nor omitting from it. In this is evidence that the scribe should be a jurist (faqih), knowledgeable in the conditions, so that what he writes comes out measured by the Sharia. It is also a command to the parties to choose the scribe, and not to appoint anyone except a jurist of piety, so that he writes only what is agreed upon. ﴿And let not the scribe refuse﴾: and let no one among the scribes refrain from writing.

﴿to write as Allah has taught him﴾: like what Allah taught him, the writing of documents, without altering or changing. The word "kamma" (as) is connected to ﴿to write﴾. ﴿So let him write﴾ that writing, and not deviate from it. ﴿And let the one who has the obligation dictate﴾: the one who dictates must be none other than the one upon whom the debt is due (p-228), because he is the one who is witnessed to the debt in his liability and his acknowledgment of it, so that this becomes an acknowledgment against himself by his own tongue. The words "imlal" and "imla'" are two dialectal forms of the same meaning.

﴿And let him fear Allah, his Lord﴾: and let the one upon whom the debt is due fear Allah, his Lord, so that he does not refuse to dictate, which would be a denial of all his right.

﴿and not diminish anything from it﴾: and let him not reduce anything of the right that is upon him in the dictation, for that would be a denial of part of the right.

﴿But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding﴾: that is, insane, because feebleness (safah) is a lightness in the intellect, or one placed under restraint (mahjur ʿalayhi) for his squandering and ignorance of how to manage affairs.

﴿or weak﴾: a child, ﴿or unable himself to dictate﴾ due to a speech impediment, or muteness, or ignorance of the language.

﴿then let his guardian dictate﴾: the one who takes charge of his affairs and manages them.

﴿with justice﴾: with truthfulness and right. ﴿And bring to witness two witnesses﴾: and seek that two witnesses testify for you concerning the debt, ﴿from among your men﴾: from among the believing men. Freedom and puberty are conditions along with Islam. The testimony of disbelievers against one another is accepted according to us.

﴿And if there are not two men﴾: if the two witnesses are not two men, ﴿then a man and two women﴾: then a man and two women shall testify. The testimony of men along with women is accepted in matters other than the hudud (fixed penalties) and qisas (retaliation).

﴿from among those whom you accept as witnesses﴾: from among those whose uprightness you know. In this is evidence that one who is not acceptable is not a witness. ﴿So that if one of them errs, the other can remind her﴾: so that if one of them forgets the testimony, the other will remind her. ("If one of them errs") is in the conditional mood; ("then remind") with the nominative and the doubled letter is the reading of Hamzah, like His words: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95]. ("then remind") with the accusative is the reading of Makki and Basri, from dhikr (remembrance), not from dhukr (mention).

﴿And let not the witnesses refuse when they are summoned﴾: for the performance of the testimony, or for taking it on, lest their rights be lost. He called them "witnesses" before they took on the testimony, treating what is about to attain a status as though it already had it. The first (refusal) is obligatory, and the second (taking it on) is recommended.

﴿And do not be weary﴾: and do not grow tired. The poet said:

*"I have grown weary of the burdens of life, and whoever lives eighty years, may you have no father, will grow weary."*

The pronoun in ﴿to write it﴾ refers to the debt or the right. ﴿Whether it be small or large﴾: whatever the right is, whether small or great. In this is evidence of the permissibility of salam in garments, because what is measured or weighed is not described as small or large; rather, that is said of things measured by length (dhar'i). It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the document, and that the writing be brief or detailed.

﴿to its term﴾: to its time, which the two creditors agreed upon naming. ﴿That﴾: a reference to ﴿to write it﴾, since it has the sense of a verbal noun, that is, "that writing."

﴿is more just﴾: more equitable than justice (qist), which is fairness.

﴿in the sight of Allah﴾: an adverbial complement of ﴿more just﴾.

﴿and more upright for testimony﴾: and more helpful in establishing the testimony. The comparative form (af'al) here, namely aqsat and aqwam, is formed from aqsaṭa and aqāma according to the school of Sibawayh.

﴿and more likely to prevent doubt﴾: and closer to the absence of doubt for the witness, the judge, and the owner of the right, for doubt may arise concerning the amount and the attributes. When they refer to the written document, that doubt is removed. The alif of "adna" is converted from a waw, because it derives from proximity (dunuww).

﴿Except when it is a present trade﴾: ʿĀṣim reads it as such, meaning: except that the trade be a trade, or except that the transaction be a present trade. Others read "tijaratun ḥāḍiratun" (a present trade) as the complete form of kāna (to occur), meaning: except that a present trade takes place. Or it is the defective form, with the subject being ﴿a present trade﴾ and the predicate ﴿you conduct﴾. ﴿Among yourselves﴾ is an adverbial complement of ﴿you conduct﴾. The meaning of conducting it among themselves is exchanging it hand to hand.

﴿There is no blame upon you if you do not write it down﴾: that is, except that you trade on the spot, hand to hand; then there is no harm in not writing it down, because there is no suspicion in it of what might be suspected in credit transactions.

﴿And take witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾: He commanded calling witnesses for sales in general, whether immediate or deferred, because that is more cautious and further from disputes. Or it is intended that "and take witnesses when you conclude a sale" refers to this kind of sale, meaning present trade, on the basis that witnessing suffices for it without writing. The command is one of recommendation.

﴿And let no scribe or witness be harmed﴾: this admits of the active voice, according to the reading of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "wa la yudarrir" (and let him not harm); and the passive voice, according to the reading of Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father: "wa la yudarrar" (and let him not be harmed) (p-230). The meaning is: the scribe and the witness are forbidden from refusing to respond to what is requested of them, and from distortion, addition, and omission; or the prohibition is against harming them, by hurrying them away from an urgent matter and pressing them, or by not giving the scribe his due wage, or by burdening the witness with the cost of travelling from another city.

﴿And if you do so﴾: and if you cause harm, ﴿then indeed it is a transgression in you﴾: indeed the harm is a sin, ﴿and fear Allah﴾: in opposing His commands. ﴿And Allah teaches you﴾: the laws of His religion. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾: He is not subject to forgetfulness or deficiency.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 283:

﴿And if you are﴾ O you who engage in debt transactions, ﴿on a journey﴾ travelling, ﴿and you do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken﴾ (fa-ruhunun) is read by Makki and Abu 'Amr. That is: that by which confidence is secured is a pledge (rihan). Both (rihan and rihun) are plurals of rahn, like saqf and suquf, and baghl and bighal. Rahn is originally a verbal noun that was named as such, then it was broken into plural like nouns. Since travel is a likely cause of the scarcity of scribes and witnesses, He commanded, by way of guidance, that one who is on a journey and wishes to preserve his property should establish security through pledging in place of security through writing and witnessing; not that travel is a condition for permitting the pledge. His saying ﴿taken into possession﴾ indicates that taking possession (al-qabd) is a condition, not as Malik claimed, that a pledge is valid by offer and acceptance without taking possession. ﴿Then if some of you trust others﴾: if some of the creditors trust some of the debtors through a good opinion of them, and so do not secure their right by writing, witnesses, or a pledge.

﴿Then let him who has been entrusted discharge his trust﴾: his debt. (The verb) iytaman is of the form ifta'ala, from al-amn (security). This is an exhortation to the debtor that he should live up to the creditor's good opinion, his sense of security in him, and his entrusting to him, and that he should pay to him the right with which he was entrusted, since he did not give a pledge against it. The debt is called a trust (amanah), and it is a guaranteed obligation, because he was entrusted with it by leaving off taking a pledge from him. ﴿And let him fear God, his Lord﴾ in denying his right. (p-231) ﴿And do not conceal testimony﴾: this is an address to the witnesses. ﴿And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾: "his heart" is raised by "sinful" as the agent, as if it were said: "his heart sins"; or by way of the inchoative, with "sinful" as a fronted predicate and the clause as the predicate of inna. It is attributed to the heart, and the whole clause is the sinful element, not the heart alone, because concealing testimony means hiding it in the heart and not speaking it. Since it is a sin committed and acquired by the heart, it is attributed to it, for attributing an act to the organ with which it is performed is more emphatic, as you say: "This is something my eye has seen, something my ear has heard, something my heart has known." Also, the heart is the chief of the organs, the lump which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. So it is as if it were said: sin has taken firm root in the origin of his self and has possessed the noblest place in it. Also, deeds of the heart are greater than deeds of the rest of the organs. Do you not see that the root of good and bad deeds is faith and disbelief, and these are deeds of the heart? And when concealing testimony is made one of the sins of the heart, it is thereby testified to be among the greatest sins. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: The greatest of the major sins are: associating partners with God, false testimony, and concealing testimony.

﴿And God is aware of what you do﴾ of concealing testimony or declaring it, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, nothing is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 284:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ — in creation and in ownership. ﴿And whether you show what is in your selves or conceal it﴾ — i.e., of evil. ﴿Allah will hold you accountable for it﴾ — He will requite you and recompense you. Whisperings (wasawis) and the discourse of the soul (hadith al-nafs) do not enter into what a person conceals, because that is something he has no capacity to be free of; rather, [what is accountable is] what he believes and resolves upon. The summary is: the resolve to disbelieve is disbelief; the passing thought of sins without resolve is forgiven; the resolve to sins, if one regrets it, turns back from it and seeks forgiveness for it, is forgiven. As for when one resolves upon an evil deed and remains firm in that, but is prevented from it by an obstacle not of his own choosing, he is not punished with the punishment of the act itself; i.e., by resolving to commit fornication he is not punished with the punishment of fornication. Is he punished with the punishment of the resolve to fornicate? It is said: No, because of the saying of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: « "Allah has overlooked for my community what their souls whisper about, so long as they do not act upon it or speak of it." » The majority hold that the reckoning concerns the passing thought, not the resolve, and that accountability for resolve is established; this is the view inclined to by Shaykh Abu Mansur and Shams al-A'imma al-Halwani, may Allah have mercy on them both. The evidence for it is the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who love that indecency should spread among those who believe...﴾ [al-Nur: 19], the verse. And from A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her: a servant who resolves upon disobedience without acting, will be punished for it by the anxiety and grief that befall him in this world. In most tafsir works it is reported that when this verse was revealed, the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were distressed and said: "Will we be held accountable for everything our souls whisper about?!" Then there was revealed: ﴿The Messenger believes...﴾ up to His saying: ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity; it has what it earned and it bears what it has earned﴾, so that accountability was tied to earning (kasb) and not to resolve. Some report that it was abrogated (nusikhat) by this verse, and the scholars of verification (al-muhaqqiqun) hold that abrogation (naskh) occurs in rulings, not in reports.

﴿So He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills﴾ — with the raising of both verbs, read by Ibn Amir and Asim, i.e., "so He forgives and punishes." With the jussive of both, read by others, as a conjunction upon the answer of the conditional clause. With idgham (assimilation), Abu Amr read it, and likewise in ﴿al-ishara﴾ and ﴿al-bishara﴾. The author of al-Kashshaf said: one who assimilates the ra' into the lam is a grammatical error and mistaken, because the ra' is a repeated letter, so it becomes like a doubled letter, and assimilation of a doubled letter is not permitted. And its transmitter from Abu Amr is mistaken twice, because he commits a solecism and attributes to the most learned of people in Arabic what indicates great ignorance.

﴿And Allah is over all things﴾ — of forgiveness, punishment and other things — ﴿Powerful﴾, capable.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 285:

﴿The Messenger believes in what has been sent down to him from his Lord, and so do the believers.﴾ If "the believers" is conjoined to "the Messenger," then the pronoun that the tanwin in ﴿kull﴾ (each) stands in for refers back to the Messenger and the believers, meaning: all of them ﴿believe in God, His angels, His books and His messengers﴾, and one pauses at that point. If, however, it is a new subject (mubtada'), then ﴿kull﴾ is a second subject, the implied construction being "each one of them," and ﴿amana﴾ (believed) is the predicate of the second subject (p-233), and the whole sentence is the predicate of the first. The pronoun then refers to the believers, and the pronoun of each one who believed is made singular in accordance with the meaning: each one of them believed. (And His book) is read by Hamza and Ali, meaning: the Qur'an, or the category (of books).

﴿We make no distinction﴾, i.e., they say, ﴿We make no distinction﴾, but rather we believe in all of them.

﴿between any of His messengers﴾. "Any" (ahad) carries the sense of a plural, and therefore "between" (bayn) governs it. It is not used with anything except a noun that denotes more than one; you say "the wealth is between the people," and you do not say "the wealth is between Zayd."

﴿And they say: We hear﴾, i.e., we answer your call, ﴿and we obey﴾ your command. ﴿Your forgiveness﴾, i.e., forgive us, your forgiveness; it is therefore in the accusative by an implied verb.

﴿Our Lord, and to You is the final return﴾, the return (al-masir). In it is an affirmation of resurrection and recompense. The verse indicates the invalidity of the exception (istithna') in faith, and that faith remains for the perpetrator of major sins.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 2, verse 286:

﴿Allah does not burden a soul⁠﴾ is either reported as their speech (maHkiyy 'anhum), or it is a new, independent statement (mustan'af).

﴿except within its capacity⁠﴾ — except within its power and ability, because obligation (taklif) only comes with an act that the one obligated is able to perform. So it is in the "Sharh al-Ta'wilat." The author of the "Kashshaf" said: al-wus' (capacity) is that which accommodates a person and does not constrict him or cause him hardship. That is, He does not burden it except with what its capacity comfortably accommodates and what is made easy for it, short of the extreme limit of its ability and effort. For it was within a person's capacity to pray more than five times, to fast more than a month, and to perform Hajj more than once.

﴿It has what it earned and upon it what it earned⁠﴾ — what it earned of good benefits it, and what it earned of evil harms it. He specified good with kasb (earning) and evil with iktisab (acquiring), because the form ifti'al (iktisab) indicates contraction and effort, and the soul contracts toward evil and exerts itself toward good.

﴿Our Lord, do not take us to task if we forget⁠﴾ — if we neglect one of Your commands out of forgetfulness — ﴿or make mistakes⁠﴾. This indicates the permissibility of being held accountable for forgetfulness and error — contrary to the Mu'tazilah — since it is possible to guard against them to a degree. And were it not permissible to be held accountable for them, the supplication would have no meaning.

﴿Our Lord, and do not lay upon us a burden (isran)⁠﴾ — a load that weighs down its bearer, i.e., holds him in place due to its heaviness. It is used metaphorically for difficult obligation, such as: killing oneself, and cutting off the place of impurity from the skin and clothing, and other such things.

﴿as You laid it upon those before us⁠﴾ — like the Jews — ﴿Our Lord, and do not burden us with what we have no strength to bear⁠﴾ — of the punishments that descended upon those before us — ﴿and pardon us⁠﴾ — erase our misdeeds — ﴿and forgive us⁠﴾ — and cover our sins. This is not a repetition: the first refers to major sins, and the second to minor sins.

﴿And have mercy upon us⁠﴾ — by making our scale heavy despite our poverty (of good deeds); or, the first is about transformation (maskh), the second about being swallowed by the earth (khasf), and the third about drowning (gharq).

﴿You are our Master (mawlana)⁠﴾ — our lord, and we are Your servants; or our helper; or the one who manages our affairs.

﴿So help us against the disbelieving people⁠﴾ — for it is the right of a master to help his servants.

In a hadith: "Whoever recites ﴿The Messenger believes⁠﴾ to the end in a night, they suffice him." And in it: "Whoever recites them after the final night prayer (al-'isha'), they suffice him in place of the night prayer (qiyam al-layl)." It is permissible to say: "I recited Surat al-Baqarah" or "I recited al-Baqarah," for what is reported from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): "The closing verses of Surat al-Baqarah are a treasure beneath the Throne." Some said: that is disliked; rather one should say: "I recited the surah in which al-Baqarah is mentioned." And Allah knows best.
